newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank Melbourne sees positive outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank Melbourne sees positive outlook.

text.p: The Bank of Melbourne said on Tuesday it saw a positive outlook for the bank's earnings for the coming six months.

"The growth of the bank in the first half gives a positive outlook for the bank's earnings for the coming six months and we anticipate continued growth in all areas of the bank in both the Victorian and interstate markets," said acting chief executive officer Robert Giles in a statement.
The Bank of Melbourne earlier announced a net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996 of A$40.1 million against A$40.02 million previously.
Chairman Christoper Stewart said the steady result was posted amid challenging market conditions for retail bankers.
Stewart said the bank's total assets grew 22.7 percent to A$11.3 billion in the half year, including A$1.2 billion of assets acquired from Westpac Banking Corp unit Challenge Bank Ltd.
Giles said the bank had successfully integrated the Challenge business, and almost all Challenge staff had joined Bank of Melbourne.
The bank now had a 16.8 percent share of the Victorian residential lending market and an 11.1 percent share of the Victorian retail deposit market, he said.
Bank of Melbourne completed the purchase of Challenge in Victoria in December for A$645 million.

The bank said total lending approvals for the half year were $A1.543 billion, up 43.7 percent on the December 1995 half result. This in part reflected interstate growth, with 40 percent of all loans now written outside Victoria.
Giles said the current competitive environment had led to a decline in the net interest margin earned by the bank, particularly in home lending.
Costs had also increased, but the bank remained one of the efficient retail banks in Australia, he said.
Operating costs as a percentage of average assets were 1.91 percent.
